questions: Did s-bend line_loss_events fall below 1.05 and s-bend progress rise above 0.64? Did any s-bend trials finish?
Did steering_oscillation rise above about 0.35 on the s-bend or oval with the narrower track and kp 2.8 combined? If so, is it controller gain or track width?

Did s-bend max_error move below the 0.06 m floor on any seed? If it stays at the floor with low oscillation, the next lever is a 0.095 m track or more turn authority from the controller, not look-ahead.
Did slalom progress recover from 0.09 toward the iteration 1 level of 0.18, and did slalom line losses stay near 1.0?
Does the oval still finish 20 of 20 with max_error near 0.025?

intent: Test whether narrowing wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m gives enough turn authority to keep the robot on the line through the s-bend. Sensors stay at y 0.07 with the same x positions and 12 mm footprint, and all other geometry is unchanged, so the only change is wheel_track. Expected result: s-bend line_loss_events below 1.0 per run, s-bend progress above 0.64, and s-bend finishes above 2 of 20. The oval should keep its 20 of 20 finish rate, and steering_oscillation should stay below about 0.35 on all tracks.
learning: Iteration 2 showed that y 0.07 fixed the slalom line losses (1.75 to 1.0) and kept the oval at 20 of 20 with lower max_error, so look-ahead is no longer the limit on the oval. The s-bend still loses the line at about 1 event per run with max_error at the floor, which points to turn authority. Narrowing the track to 0.09 m is the next test. Slalom progress fell from 0.18 to 0.09 at y 0.07, so watch whether that is lag or noise.
rationale: Iteration 2 (score 433, up from 389) moved the sensors to y 0.07 with wheel_track 0.10. The oval now finishes 20 of 20 (mean max_error 0.0255, down from 0.035), so the extra look-ahead is not adding lag and y 0.07 stays. Slalom line losses fell from 1.75 to 1.0 per run, so the footprint-widening fallback (sensor_size 0.016) is not triggered. The s-bend is still the binding problem: 18 of 20 trials go off track at progress 0.64, max_error sits at the 0.06 m floor (0.0597), line_loss_events is 1.05 per run, and steering_oscillation is 0.299. That meets the Integrator's stated trigger: line loss near 1.0, max_error at the floor, and oscillation below about 0.3. Following that rule, I narrow wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m. This raises turn rate per unit wheel difference by about 1.11x, which should add turn authority on the s-bend. The main risk is that oscillation rises past 0.3 once the Integrator's kp rise to 2.8 is combined with the narrower track. I keep sensor y at 0.07 (not 0.08) because the oval shows no lag yet, and I keep sensor_size 0.012, x positions, wheel radius, body and mass fixed so the only geometric change is wheel_track. Expected result: s-bend finish rate and progress rise (progress above 0.64), with line_loss_events falling below 1.0 and max_error dropping below the 0.06 floor on some seeds. The oval should keep finishing. If oscillation exceeds about 0.35 on the s-bend, the next step is an intermediate wheel_track of 0.095 rather than further narrowing.
